paragraphs.source_en: 3. After verifying the message and destination with the customer, the operator pushes a button which automatically sends the message to a master computer in Middletown, Virginia. 4. The computer processes the message and relays it to an earth station in Glenwood, New Jersey. 5. From there the message goes up in space 22,300 miles to a Westar satellite in synchronous orbit about the equator. This is the Westar satellite that played a key role in the Mailgram system. Later we tried strenuously to get Western Union to change its name to Westar Corporation. They refused and later the company went bankrupt. Would a name change have helped? We think so. (Today, of course, the Western Union brand survives as a money transfer service, a shadow of its former glory.)
